speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is causing your discomfort, tell me if you are having trouble passing stool or if your stools look like pellets?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the information; the tenderness and distension suggest significant abdominal pain. Has the baby been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or bile-stained?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound results show normal readings, which is helpful. Is the baby passing any stool at all, or is he completely constipated with no gas or feces coming out?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since there has been no vomiting or diarrhea, and the ultrasound is normal, I need to rule out an intestinal obstruction. Has the baby ever passed meconium (the first stool) within the first 24 hours after birth, and is he currently passing any gas?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms a high-grade intestinal obstruction with dilated bowel loops and an empty rectum. Since the meconium passage history and ultrasound were inconclusive, has there been a family history of Hirschsprung's disease in any relatives? Also, please tell me if the baby passed his first stool within the first 24 hours of life.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
